answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Each player starts with 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the designated spaces. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 as hand cards and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Place the Animals Action card under the leftmost slot (strength 1); shuffle the other four Action cards among the remaining slots; all begin side I up. 6. Appeal starts at 0 for the start player, 1 for second, 2 for third and 3 for fourth in turn order.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; 1 active and 3 inactive workers; 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8, keep 4; Animals under slot 1, remaining 4 random; appeal staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. In a four-player game, place the top 4 shuffled Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; in games with 2 or 3 players, place the top 3. 2. In a two-player game only, block one level on each of the three face-up base projects (left on left card, middle on middle card, right on right card) and the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column; these spaces cannot be used by either player. 3. No project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup with three or four players. 4. Keep the initial 6-card Zoo-card display face down until all players have chosen their starting hands, then reveal it.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c specifies 4 projects at four players, otherwise 3, and the two-player blocked levels/donation column; setup G reveals display after hand choice.

answers.answer: 1. After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were left of the empty slot one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before performing the action; slot position sets base strength and each X-token spent beforehand adds 1 strength. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that action, though earlier action benefits may be used in later steps. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an effect labeled ‘after finishing’ only after the action is complete, including moving its Action card.
answers.evidence: Turn structure: remove used card, shift all cards left of empty slot right, place used card in slot 1. X-tokens: set strength before; maximum 5. ‘After finishing’ effects follow card movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not do nothing; playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal regular action. 2. Instead, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. 3. Move that selected card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right as usual. 4. You cannot take this alternative if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure prohibits doing nothing; X-token action says take exactly 1, move card to slot 1, strength/upgrade irrelevant, unavailable at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond that space and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 2. The break occurs after the triggering player's current turn is completed. 3. Play resumes clockwise after the break with the next player; the Break token resets to the starting space for the player count.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn’; gain 1 X-token; ignore additional steps; after break token returns to start and play continues clockwise.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I: advance the Break token 2 spaces without taking money, then choose either to draw from the deck according to the strength table (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 card of your choice from the display regardless of reputation; a snap is not combined with a deck draw. 2. Cards II: advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or from display folders within reputation range in any order using the side-II table; at strength 5 the example is 4 cards and discard 1. 3. Side-II snap works at strength 3 or more, takes exactly one display card of any reputation and no deck cards; the reputation restriction only limits the side-II draw option. 4. Cards taken from the display are not replenished until the turn ends. 5. Hand limit is checked at breaks only, not during the turn.
answers.evidence: CARDS action and Special Rules: both sides advance Break 2; side-I snap at 5, side-II snap at 3; snapping any-reputation; no in-turn hand limit; display replenishment at turn end.

answers.answer: 1. ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action; upgrading Cards also unlocks progress past 9. 3. At reputation 15, additional reputation leaves the counter at 15 and converts each remaining step to 1 appeal. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track: within range is matching folder and lower folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: 1. Build I constructs exactly 1 building, of size no greater than action strength. Build II constructs any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but never two identical buildings in the same Build action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a border space; later buildings must touch an existing building along at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces within the map; do not overlap buildings or cover water/rock. Build-restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, only once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: I exactly one, II different buildings total size up to strength; 2 money/space. Placement rules specify border first, adjacency later, restricted icon, kiosk spacing; pavilion gives appeal 1.

answers.answer: 1. Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo; a Petting Zoo is size 3 and each zoo may have at most one. 2. Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo; each is size 5. There are four tiles of each special enclosure type in the supply, one per player. 3. Build cannot construct unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal; Build II is needed to cover restricted-icon spaces, though other effects may also complete the map.
answers.evidence: Buildings table and Build sections list available buildings and one-per-zoo special enclosure limits; unique buildings only via Sponsors; full map grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Earlier bonuses gained during an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that same action; resolve items one at a time. 2. Pay for each item before receiving the benefits belonging to that item (for example, an animal's money-gain effect cannot pay its own cost). 3. Immediate effects resolve when triggered; an ‘after finishing’ effect waits until the entire action is completed and its Action card has moved. 4. If simultaneous effects occur, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-token/general turn rules permit earlier action bonuses in later steps and require payment before own benefits; action/card rules defer ‘after finishing’; simultaneous effects order chosen by owner.

answers.answer: 1. To play an Animal, satisfy every left-side condition, pay its printed cost, and house it legally. A matching partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon printed on the Animal card, so a double icon reduces it by 6. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; the animal normally goes alone there and the whole enclosure flips to occupied. Petting Zoo animals can only use a Petting Zoo. 3. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their indicated Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary alternative, putting one supply player token per required space; the special enclosure is not flipped and may hold multiple animals if combined needs fit capacity. 4. Meet required water/rock adjacency for the chosen enclosure; count distinct adjacent hexes, not multiple touching edges to the same hex. 5. Resolve normal effects immediately after housing/card placement; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until all animals in the action are played and the Animals card has moved. Costs must be paid before any gain-money effect pays.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps 1–5; partner zoo discount is 3 per continent icon; enclosure table and special capacity; terrain distinct adjacent hexes; after-finishing timing.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits playing Animal cards from display folders within your reputation range, in addition to hand cards. 2. Pay an added cost equal to the display folder number for each display Animal. 3. At strength 5 or more, you may choose to gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to the Animals you play. 4. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 5. Animals II permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II paragraph specifies in-range display animals, folder-number cost, optional reputation first at strength 5+, delayed refill and upgrade-conditioned animals.

answers.answer: 1. Relocation is available only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, once for that newly built building; eligible corresponding animals that fit may be moved, choosing each separately, and all that fit may be moved. 2. Add the indicated number of player tokens from your supply to the new special enclosure for each moved animal; total marked capacity cannot exceed its five spaces. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that satisfies all that animal's requirements, including terrain, to empty. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even its size, flip none. 4. The new special enclosure must itself satisfy the animal's water/rock adjacency and have enough free capacity.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals section: only immediately on construction; move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, separately; add indicated tokens; smallest all-requirements enclosure, then size-only fallback, else none.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks have these strengths: increase reputation 2; gain a partner zoo 3; gain a university 4; conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task, requiring total action strength at least the task's strength. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed action strength. 3. Place 1 active worker on a task; if one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers instead; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot do it again until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action lists task strengths and worker requirement; side II states different tasks and total value; repeating task requires two own workers; three own workers blocks; other players do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; do not take them directly from general supply. 2. Take any printed covered-space bonus immediately. When taking a university, also immediately take its printed reputation award, if any. 3. You cannot take a duplicate university; all partner zoos must be different continents and a zoo can have at most four. The third and fourth partner zoos require Association II. 4. Universities provide research icons and may award reputation; only the hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5. University types already owned by every player are not restocked at breaks; otherwise restock one tile of each kind without adding duplicates.
answers.evidence: Association task details and University tiles/setup: acquire from board to lowest empty map spaces, bonuses; no duplicate universities; partner limits; 3rd requires II; hand limit university raises to 5.

answers.answer: 1. At conservation project work, either support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II can use an in-range display project for its folder-number cost. A new project goes above the board at the left, shifting others right. 2. Fulfill a printed condition and choose a reward level with no player's token on it; each level holds one token total, and you normally may support each project only once (never one already bearing your token). 3. Take one support token from the left edge of your zoo map, put it on that condition, gain its depicted conservation/reputation, and activate the uncovered map bonus immediately (before or after project reward, your choice); recurring income repeats at every break. 4. When project cards overflow the above-board limit, discard the rightmost; tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses remain activated. The fixed base projects below the board never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work gives sources, placement, overflow, separate support limits and four-step support procedure; map bonuses activated and recurring.

answers.answer: 1. No: release matching uses the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement by category: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts 3, and 4+ accepts 4 or 5. The actual occupied enclosure or special-enclosure capacity does not define the category. 2. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; later support of one already in play does not. 3. If the released animal could live in a special enclosure and the required number of its tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all animal requirements including terrain; if none does, the smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. This applies to flock animals too.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild paragraph sets printed-size bands, loss/retention order, new-card reputation and special-token removal/standard-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand; action strength must be at least its level and conditions must be met. Alternatively, advance the Break token by strength and gain that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play multiple Sponsors from hand and/or display within reputation range; strength plus 1 must be at least the sum of their levels. Pay each display card's folder number extra; refill display only at turn end. II allows upgrade-conditioned cards. 3. Resolve cards one after another, fully resolving each card's immediate effects before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4. If instead taking the break/money option on II, gain money twice the action strength, even if the Break token has fewer spaces before the end; on I the full strength amount is also paid even when fewer spaces remain.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS I/II descriptions state budgets, sources, costs, conditions, sequencing and double money; side-I money is full strength even if token does not need all steps.

answers.answer: 1. Break steps are: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock available partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact remaining cards and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do. 3. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve affected players clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them); refill the display after each such player's income and before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 and kiosk income definition; break-income ordering paragraph specifies clockwise order and refill after each affected player.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose either to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus tile beside that space (the 5-money option remains when tiles are gone). The first time any player reaches 10, all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before end scoring. 2. Check for game end only at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. If another player's turn gives you appeal, your zoo waits until the end of your own turn or a break to check. 3. If triggered at the end of a player's turn, that player completes it and every other player gets one final turn; if triggered during a break, all players get one final turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can provide at most 4 conservation points. Target Number is the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; VP = Appeal minus Target Number. Highest positive VP wins; tie goes to the tied player with most supported projects (tokens removed from map); remaining tie is shared.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory and Official FAQ specify 2/5/8/10 rewards, end-check timing and final turns, 4-point per-card cap, VP formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place a random face-up tile on each of the 4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two at 5 conservation and two at 8; do not put tiles on the two yellow icon spaces and return the remaining 5 tiles to the box. 2. Components are not legally limiting: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Setup places 4 random Bonus tiles on blank spaces at 5/8; component supply rule says use suitable substitute if a component runs out.

answers.answer: 1. Advanced Maps 1–8 are reverse sides with individual abilities. Choose 2 random zoo maps and keep 1 advanced map, or lay out player count plus 1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A begins with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and is covered with a kiosk tile as reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A describes advanced map selection options and Map A's starting enclosure and kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. The 7 support tokens start on the designated spaces along the left edge of each zoo map; each is taken to support a conservation project and its uncovered bonus activates. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; Full-throated likewise directs taking a printed last-worker conservation reward.
answers.evidence: Your zoo map section places 7 tokens at left edge; worker rule says lowest reserve worker first and certain maps grant conservation when last hired.

answers.answer: 1. Flip one Action card from side I to side II when gaining an upgrade; it stays in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is available starting with your next action, but the card immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards; one upgrade source lets you choose an alternative, so not all can be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards paragraph gives position, next-action use, immediate condition status and the four sources with one alternative.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I at strength 1 draws 1 and discards 1; strength 2 draws 1 and discards 0; strength 3 draws 2 and discards 1; strength 4 draws 2 and discards 0; strength 5 or more draws 3 and discards 1. 2. A required discard may be either a newly drawn card or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw table gives side-I draw/discard sequence; table note says required discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. The animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when also shown with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is also its own category. Include both unless an effect explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: seven animal categories; bear remains a category; Petting Zoo animal is its own category.

answers.answer: 1. Donation is available only during Association II after at least one association task in the same action; it needs no worker and is limited to exactly 1 donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area and cover that space with a token from your supply; gain 1 conservation point. 3. The printed costs in order are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10 and 10 money, followed by a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once every space but the last is covered, later donations cost 12 money and place no further token.
answers.evidence: Association II donation paragraph states qualifying task, worker status, one-per-action limit, visible cost, token/reward, sequence and repeatable final cost.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, plus water/rock requirement icons in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards; also count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. University reputation and hand-limit marks are benefits, not icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons. A card counts its own icon for its effects; doubled icons count twice. When asked for different icon types, repeated copies count as one type. 3. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo lists counted/not-counted icons and own-card/double behavior; glossary says card text takes priority.

answers.answer: 1. Water/rock requirements count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; multiple edges touching the same terrain hex count once. A larger connected water/rock region contributes only the hexes actually adjacent to the chosen enclosure, so a two-space requirement needs two distinct adjacent hexes. 2. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not count.
answers.evidence: Animal requirements and glossary: count distinct adjacent hexes; larger terrain area counts only actually adjacent hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild Conservation Project card grants 1 reputation; supporting a Release project already in play does not grant that play bonus. 2. For all Breeding Program project cards 123–127, the condition is the same at all three reward spaces on a given card; after meeting it, choose any available reward space, including for the Reptile example.
answers.evidence: Release project rules distinguish new-card reputation from later support; Breeding Program clarification gives same condition at all three levels and any available space.

answers.answer: 1. In an effect written X:Y, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition with no number, or with ‘per,’ pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds are listed, use only the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Glossary: X on left is condition, Y reward; condition without number/per pays once per fulfillment; numbered thresholds pay once and use highest met.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes these for all players.
answers.evidence: Glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. A unique building must be placed when its Sponsor is played; if it cannot legally fit, that Sponsor card cannot be played. 2. Place the matching tile with its colored face up, rotate it freely but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement rules and any printed water/rock adjacency requirement. 3. No size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique-building glossary rules state required placement, orientation, ordinary rules/terrain, no size payment, and no enclosure/terrain function.

answers.answer: 1. For both a named Action and Determination (Any Action), finish the Animals action, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking the granted action. 2. Use the granted action's own Action card normally and move that card to slot 1 after the granted action. 3. A named Action must be performed as named and cannot be replaced with the X-token alternative; Determination may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications specify shared timing and card movement; named action cannot substitute X-token, Determination can.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project to hand; Dominance takes its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play the obtained card through Association and support it immediately; it enters above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below it.
answers.evidence: Assertion/Dominance clarification specifies source, duplicate case, and later play/support above board.

answers.answer: 1. Both Boost and Clever resolve after the Animals action finishes and its Animals card moves to slot 1. 2. Clever puts the chosen card into slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card into slot 1 or slot 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost/Clever clarification states timing, allowed slots and card-shifting directions.

answers.answer: 1. The target eligibility floor for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction is at least 5 appeal for each affected zoo. 2. The Animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability, so its new appeal normally does not have to count when selecting affected players. 3. The multiplayer group may replace the interactive ability with the alternative text marked for solo on those cards; this does not require playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities section gives common 5-appeal eligibility, timing of playing animal appeal, and multiplayer alternative text.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction affects other eligible zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: ahead on one track gets one token on your slot-5 card; ahead on both gets two tokens on your slot-4 and slot-5 cards. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2. Each token reduces the affected card's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 3. Remove the token after using that card, or at the break if unused; break clearing makes unused tokens have no effect.
answers.evidence: Interactive target table and Constriction paragraph give target count, slots, no stacking, -2 strength, multiplied application, removal.

answers.answer: 1. At effective strength 0 or less, you cannot take an ordinary action at that strength; you must spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The X-token alternative can be used only if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Constriction says at zero or below, boost to at least one, use alternative X-token action, or leave until slot 3; X-token action is unavailable at 5.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card and drawing one deck card; decide anew after each card, so choices may differ. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification states up to twice, choose again after each card, and immediate display replacement/compaction.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal avoids occupying a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join the flock animal in the flock animal's enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, you still free an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure; historical proof of exactly where it was first housed is not tracked.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification specifies host size/category, unlimited reuse, no later non-flock sharing, and release/fallback without historical residents.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it onto the notepad for immediate use. 2. If your map grants conservation for hiring your last worker, take that printed reward. 3. If all workers are already active, Full-throated has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification states reserve order, last-worker conservation and no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, keeps one revealed Animal card and discards the rest. If none revealed is an Animal card, discard all revealed cards and add none to hand.
answers.evidence: Hunter X clarification: reveal X, add one Animal, discard others; with no Animal, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Choose among tied highest-appeal eligible targets; if you yourself are the target, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. You may copy only a card in the target's slot 1, 2 or 3. Use that card's owner's upgraded or unupgraded side for the entire copied action, but use your own X-tokens and your own Action cards for other upgrade checks. 3. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally. Venom and Constriction on the copied card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification specifies tie/self target, slots, target-side upgrade, own X-tokens, movement and tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Put an earned Multiplier on the specifically named Action card, or, if gained from a Bonus tile, choose any Action card including Animals. 2. On its next use, you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength and move the card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions finish; a break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn finishes and does not stop the second execution. 4. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier section states placement by reward source, two executions, one X per execution, deferred effects, break timing and token return.

answers.answer: 1. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three executions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token holding limit. 3. You cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action within the multiplied use.
answers.evidence: Multiplier choices: additional token adds one execution; two tokens mean up to three; X-token action can be multiplied but cannot mix with regular action.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking lets you place a Large Bird Aviary before upgrading Build, provided your zoo does not already have an Aviary and a legal site exists. 2. Other placement restrictions remain, including needing Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces. 3. Posturing placements follow normal rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking says Aviary may be placed before Build upgrade subject to no existing Aviary/legal site and restricted-space Build II; Posturing clarifies ordinary rules and sequential placement.

answers.answer: 1. The first Petting Zoo animal grants 3 appeal, the second 6, and the third 9. 2. A zoo has one Petting Zoo, holding at most 3 such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal ability: first/second/third give 3/6/9 appeal; one Petting Zoo holds at most three; they count as small.

answers.answer: 1. For Pilfering 1, choose among ties for highest-appeal eligible target; self-target has no effect. 2. For Pilfering 2, resolve highest-appeal and most-conservation targets separately, choosing among ties; a conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. If the same zoo leads both, it is pilfered twice. 3. Each target must have at least 5 appeal; if all players have zero conservation, the conservation-target part has no effect, but the separate highest-appeal part may still resolve under its floor and self-target rule.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X clarification resolves highest appeal and conservation separately, tie/self behavior, 5-appeal floor, and zero-conservation case.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. With no hand cards, the target gives 5 money; with less than 5 money, the target gives a card. If the target has neither a card nor 5 money, give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings one after another, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X paragraph states target choice, no Final Scoring cards, fallback cases and sequential repeated choices.

answers.answer: 1. Cards tucked under an animal by Pouch have no remaining function. If that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, but keep the appeal already gained from tucking them. 2. Cards sold through Sunbathing go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarification specifies no further function, release discard/retained appeal, and sold cards to discard pile.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you choose one to discard at that milestone. 2. At game end score every Final Scoring card remaining; each is separately capped at 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification says extra card joins milestone choices and every remaining card scores subject to its own four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the card's stated selection, then returns the discard pile face up. For the illustrated Scavenging 3, draw three random discard cards, keep one and discard the other two.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification states shuffle face down, random draw, selection and return face up; illustrated 3 keeps one of three.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors without a reputation-range restriction; if no Sponsor is present, it has no effect. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping/Sponsor Magnet clarification gives exact source, reputation rule, empty result and ordinary refill timing.

answers.answer: 1. Put Venom tokens on the affected player's Action cards starting in the lowest slots (1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn; this includes the X-token alternative if you have fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one Venom token remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose a different action; spending all your money cannot evade the fee. 4. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X clarification specifies placement, no stacking, using marked card, conditional fee and failure procedure, and break expiration.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian 203 immediately gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities, respectively. 2. Its recurring effect lowers the strength required to support Conservation Projects from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring reward is 1 conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 203 Veterinarian lists immediate money tiers, project strength 4 and one conservation for three universities.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough 206 immediately gives 2 appeal per previously supported project, counted by the number of support tokens missing from the left edge of your map. 2. It gives 1 conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 206: appeal per previously supported project (missing map tokens); break income 1 conservation.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research 207 counts different continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research icons; each type counts once even if repeated or doubled. 2. Its owner gains 1 conservation per two distinct types, rounding down. 3. Every other player gains 2 money for each conservation point the owner gains.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 207 specifies types included/excluded, unique type count, rounded-down reward and other-player money.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library 208 immediately gives 1 appeal per research icon. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation for having five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 208 lists immediate appeal, owner reward whenever any player plays research, and final category condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas 210 immediately gives 1 appeal per Americas icon. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, subject to ordinary placement and kiosk-spacing restrictions. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 210 lists immediate appeal per icon, free kiosk under normal placement/spacing and five-kiosk final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia 212 immediately gives 1 appeal per Australia icon. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath the Sponsor for 2 appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 212 states immediate appeal and one tucked hand card per icon for 2 appeal, with tucked cards having no further function.

answers.answer: 1. When played, Global Breeding Program 215 or Breeding Program 218 takes two player tokens from your supply and places them on its two printed spaces. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one token from this Sponsor to your supply as any one icon; you cannot spend both tokens on one project. 3. Base-origin projects played above the board do not qualify. 4. Final reward: 1 conservation for five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 215/218 specifies two stored supply tokens, one substitute on below-board base projects, no double use/above-board projects, final support count.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer 217 allows each Build action to include one extra copy of a building already built in that same action, without additional strength. 2. Pay the normal money and follow normal placement rules; special enclosures still have a one-per-type zoo limit. Only one extra building is allowed even if the action builds several different types. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 217 describes one extra copy, no added strength, normal payment/placement and special limit; final appeal condition.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher 219 immediately gives 2 money per water/rock icon. 2. It permits covering water/rock spaces and ignoring terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. 3. Terrain need not be covered for full-map status, but covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo. 4. It scores 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 219 details money, terrain permission/requirements, effects on other scoring and final pair scoring.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist 221 triggers whenever an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. For each such bonus, gain an additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, which need not be on the border; multiple triggers may choose the same bonus or different bonuses. Resolve choices in any order. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 221 specifies trigger, any uncovered bonus, repeated choices same/different and final border condition.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording 224 immediately gives 1 X-token. 2. Each Release into the Wild support grants 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly using different qualifying animals, but at most once per project in a single Association action. 3. Each placed support token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 224 states immediate X-token, extra conservation per release support, repeated different animals with per-action limit and separate counting.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab 225 immediately gives 1 X-token. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation with all five continent icons.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 225 lists token, four immunities and target redirection for two effects, plus final condition.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Special Assignment 227 lets you permanently choose small or large and mark that choice with a supply token; reveal Zoo cards until finding an animal of the chosen type, keep it and discard the others. 2. You cannot play animals of the opposite size category. 3. From then on chosen small animals grant 2 extra appeal or chosen large animals grant 4 extra appeal. Size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 227 states permanent type selection, reveal/keep procedure, prohibition, bonuses and size-3 exception.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program 228 immediately gives 2 money per small animal. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals may play one additional small Animal from hand with normal costs/rules; mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents this extra-play effect. 3. The ability then allows taking one small Animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation, even if you declined the extra play.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 228 states immediate money, all-small action condition, extra hand animal and display animal regardless of reputation even if extra play declined.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist 241 immediately gives 1 appeal per water icon. 2. Its recurring effect pays 1 money for each space newly covered adjacent to water, even when multiple spaces are part of one building; adjacency to several water hexes still pays only once for that space. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected (none isolated).
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 241 lists appeal, per-space building trigger with one payment per space, and connected-water final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut 249 is a Sponsor that places its unique building in the zoo under ordinary placement rules. 2. Whenever a bird icon is played, its recurring effect draws two cards from the deck; keep one and discard the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 249: place unique building; each bird icon played draws two deck cards, keeps one, discards other.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank 250 is placed as a unique building adjacent to water. 2. Each time a reptile icon is played, its recurring effect lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money apiece; discard sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 250 specifies water adjacency and reptile-triggered sale of up to two cards at 4 money each to discard.

answers.answer: 1. Spotted Hyena Compound 252 triggers Hunter when a predator icon is played, with the number of cards revealed equal to your total predator icons. 2. If the newly played card has two predator icons, trigger two Hunters sequentially, counting the new predator icons for each calculation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 252 states each predator icon triggers Hunter with draws based on total predator icons; double icon triggers two sequential Hunters, counting new icons each time.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable 253 enters play with three player tokens from your supply on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a Sponsor in your hand's level to play that Sponsor, subject to its normal conditions. 3. Its own herbivore icon can trigger the effect immediately when the Stable is played. There are three uses total.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 253 gives three tokens, one per herbivore trigger, money equal to hand Sponsor level and normal conditions, including own icon trigger.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School 254 immediately grants 1 reputation and 1 conservation and lets you take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 254 lists reputation/conservation, building must cover two border spaces, card choice and chosen order for simultaneous benefits.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance 257 is placed as a unique building on two border spaces and does not need to touch an existing building; later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building, excluding empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. As a unique building it counts as a qualifying neighbor for adjacent kiosks' income. 4. Final reward: 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 257 gives two-border placement exception, income neighbor definition, kiosk cross-income and full-map appeal reward.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals 260 immediately gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces never count. 2. At final scoring gain 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately and adding the group scores. 3. Build-restricted spaces count even when Build is not upgraded; water and rock spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 260 specifies connected uncovered building border spaces and final empty-space groups; restricted spaces included and terrain excluded.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer 262 immediately gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon type; research icons do not count. 2. Its recurring effect gives 1 appeal and 2 money for each continent/category type newly introduced to your zoo. 3. A double of the same newly introduced icon type earns this novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 262 lists immediate distinct icon types excluding research and recurring newly introduced category/continent; identical double triggers novelty once.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program 263 immediately permits placing one size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. Its recurring effect when playing a large animal allows ignoring one left-side condition, such as one required icon or Animals-upgrade requirement; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 263 states free size-5 enclosure, one left-side condition waiver, terrain exception, and stacking with Research Institute.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo 009 compares each animal category's icon count in your zoo with the player to your right; gain 1 conservation for each category where you have more icons. 2. If they have zero of a category, at least one of your icons wins that category. 3. Maximum reward is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring clarifications: 1 conservation for each category with more icons than player right, including zero case, maximum 4.

answers.answer: 1. Map 1 Observation Tower grants its bonus only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. If an animal is later released and the standard enclosure emptied/refilled, housing an animal there grants the two appeal again. 4. The Tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 clarification names tower-hex adjacency, standard-only bonus, repeat on rehousing after release and not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Map 2 Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not just another water hex. 2. After placement, that enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. 3. You cannot ignore the size increase for release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Areas is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 clarification gives qualifying hex, +2 size for all purposes including release/transfer, special-enclosure exception and not a building.

answers.answer: 1. A building on the space adjacent to Map 4 Commercial Harbor activates it; your first building may start beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Use its discard ability before, during or after your action, at most once on your own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 clarification states activation, first-building option, ability timing/limit, and Harbor is not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Map 5 Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, not per building; empty enclosures qualify, and multiple spaces of one building each count. 2. The Restaurant is not a building, but adjacent kiosks count it as a unique building for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus grants one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and obey all other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 clarification defines per-covered-hex income, says Restaurant is not a building, and allows one of either special enclosure free before Build II.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 8 Hollywood Hills, cover H spaces with buildings under ordinary placement rules. When covering an H, reveal Zoo cards until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II to cover upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 clarification states ordinary placement, reveal/keep Sponsor, no Archaeologist trigger, level reduction and persistent upgrade restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its ordinary conditions. 2. This bonus effect plays the Sponsor only from your hand, even if Sponsors II is upgraded; it cannot use the display. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ bonus Sponsor effect: cost equals level, normal conditions, hand only even with Sponsors II, Sponsors card remains in slot.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and Conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond either track's end are lost. 2. Reputation has a separate overflow rule: once at 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ states Appeal cap 113 and Conservation cap 41 with excess lost; Reputation track gives appeal overflow at 15.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal, choosing among ties; if that is your own zoo, it has no effect, and it copies only slot 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation, with each target at least 5 appeal and a conservation target needing at least 1 conservation; choose among ties and self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: one track ahead means one token, both means two tokens. All interactive affected zoos have the 5-appeal floor.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference gives target rules for each named ability and shared 5-appeal floor; Constriction explains one/two tokens.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from that Animal's continent; a Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition permits any continent. 2. A left-side maximum-25-appeal condition allows play only while your zoo has no more than 25 appeal; the marker at 25 is a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-side requirement (such as a required icon or Animals-upgrade condition), but does not remove terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ clarifies Animal vs Sponsor partner conditions, max-25 condition, minimum reputation and ignore-condition bonus excluding terrain.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 gives up to two selections, each choosing between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding one hand card and drawing one deck card. 2. You may choose either option each time and decide again after the first selection.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification says choose up to twice between the two options and decide again after each card.

answers.answer: 1. When replenishing a display after cards are taken, move higher-numbered remaining cards down in their existing order to fill gaps. 2. Then fill empty spaces from the deck. 3. When display cards are discarded by Digging, the card is replaced immediately by shifting folders down and drawing into folder 6; ordinary action display refill otherwise waits until turn end. The break separately discards folders 1 and 2, compacts, and refills.
answers.evidence: Reputation/display paragraph says move cards from higher folders down keeping order and fill empties; Digging and break rules specify their respective refill timing.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures with the empty side up, showing the yellow edge and size number. 2. Each covered placement-bonus space grants its bonus immediately, once; resolve all bonuses for a building before the next building. 3. Turning the enclosure occupied later does not award the covered placement bonus again.
answers.evidence: Build action states empty side up; placement bonus immediately once; standard enclosure occupancy later does not repeat it.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches 10 conservation, every player chooses and discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring deck/pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation track 10-point reward: all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; ordinary play proceeds clockwise. 2. The game does not use formal rounds; players take turns one at a time until an end trigger. 3. On each turn perform one action using one of the five Action cards; additional effects or bonuses may grant further actions after the base action under their own timing rules.
answers.evidence: Setup randomly determines start player, clockwise; Overview says no formal rounds; Turn Structure says one action per turn and ability clarifications cover granted actions after finishing.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, every player must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: Conservation 10-point rule: if no one reaches 10 before game ends, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
